Whether a fit has converged

Source: R/kb_converged.R
kb_converged.Rd

Whether a model fit has converged, from the Rhat and effective sample sizes of its parameters and its rate of divergent transitions.

Usage

kb_converged(fit, ..., rhat = 1.01, ess = 100, max_perc_divergent = 0.2)

Arguments

fit

A kb_fit object.

...

These dots are for future extensions and must be empty.

rhat

A number giving the maximum acceptable Rhat.

ess

A number giving the minimum acceptable bulk and tail effective sample size per chain.

max_perc_divergent

A number giving the maximum acceptable percentage of saved draws that ended in a divergent transition.

Value

A flag: TRUE if all three conditions are met, otherwise FALSE.

Assessing convergence

Three conditions must be met:

  • every parameter's rank-normalized split Rhat below rhat (default 1.01; Vehtari et al. 2021, Section 2);

  • every parameter's bulk and tail effective sample size at least ess times the number of chains (default 100, which is 400 for four chains; Vehtari et al. 2021);

  • the percentage of divergent transitions at or below max_perc_divergent (default 0.2% of saved draws). Set max_perc_divergent = 0 to require none.

Rhat and the effective sample sizes are those of posterior::rhat(), posterior::ess_bulk(), and posterior::ess_tail(), reported for each parameter by posterior::summarise_draws(fit).

Resolving convergence failure

In order, try the following:

  1. For Rhat or effective sample sizes that fail their thresholds, increase nthin to run more iterations while saving the same number of draws or increase niters for more saved draws per chain.

  2. For divergent transitions, increase adapt_delta through the control argument of the kb_fit_*() functions (for example, kb_fit_*(df, control = list(adapt_delta = 0.99)); the default is 0.95). A higher value makes the sampler take smaller steps, which reduces divergent transitions at the cost of a longer runtime.

  3. If either problem persists, check the data and the fit with pp_check() and kb_influence(): a unit mistake, outliers, or a poor fit can cause both.

References

Vehtari, A., Gelman, A., Simpson, D., Carpenter, B., and Bürkner, P.-C. (2021). Rank-normalization, folding, and localization: An improved \(\widehat{R}\) for assessing convergence of MCMC. Bayesian Analysis, 16(2), 667-718. doi:10.1214/20-BA1221

Stan Development Team. Runtime warnings and convergence problems. https://mc-stan.org/learn-stan/diagnostics-warnings.html

See also

Other diagnostics: kb_influence(), kb_plot_trace(), kb_sensitivity(), loo.kb_fit(), pp_check.kb_fit()

Examples

kb_converged(fit_weight_sim_nereo)
#> [1] TRUE

# Require no divergent transitions at all:
kb_converged(fit_weight_sim_nereo, max_perc_divergent = 0)
#> [1] TRUE
